title: Equal people, unequal portions
hook: Two full portions and one half portion: what does one full portion represent?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Calculate a weighted share and distinguish it from equal-person division.

misconception: Equal headcounts and equal consumption weights always produce the same split.
objective: Calculate a weighted share and distinguish it from equal-person division.

claims.text: Two full portions and one half portion total 2.5 portion units. A splits by units; B by three people. Scaled model; fictional bill; agreed portion weights.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Bill=30€, A=€12 and B=€10. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",2.5]; B=["/","x",3]; x denotes Bill. At x=30, A=12, B=10; recall at x=33: B=11. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: A weighted split divides by 2.5 portion units rather than three people. A full portion gets one unit; the half portion gets half a unit. This is arithmetic under an agreed rule, not a recommendation for splitting bills.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",2.5]; B=["/","x",3]; x denotes Bill. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: Two full portions and one half portion total 2.5 portion units. A splits by units; B by three people. Change only Bill to 33€. What is B (Equal-people) now? Correct: €11. Use B's stated rule with Bill=33€: it gives €11. A weighted split divides by 2.5 portion units rather than three people. A full portion gets one unit; the half portion gets half a unit. This is arithmetic under an agreed rule, not a recommendation for splitting bills.

recall.question: Two full portions and one half portion total 2.5 portion units. A splits by units; B by three people. Change only Bill to 33€. What is B (Equal-people) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Bill=33€: it gives €11. A weighted split divides by 2.5 portion units rather than three people. A full portion gets one unit; the half portion gets half a unit. This is arithmetic under an agreed rule, not a recommendation for splitting bills.
